subtopic: GQA / Compute vs memory trade-off across variants
learningObjective: Distinguish how MQA/GQA affect KV memory, decode compute, and quality relative to MHA.
stem: Select all statements that are correct about GQA (Grouped Query Attention) relative to MHA and MQA. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: GQA is typically found to preserve model quality better than MQA, at the cost of using more KV memory than MQA but still much less than MHA.

GQA cannot be applied to a pretrained MHA model without full retraining, because the arrangement of KV heads is a topological property of the attention operator that is not amenable to post-hoc adaptation.
GQA reduces per-token KV cache to 2 * G * d per layer (G = number of KV groups), which for typical G = H/8 or H/4 gives 4-8x KV footprint reduction over MHA.
GQA reduces total attention FLOPs at inference by the same factor as it reduces KV heads, because each query head only needs to compute attention against a subset of KV heads.

explanation: A is correct: GQA groups H query heads into G KV groups; per-token KV cache is 2*G*d per layer, and typical H/G ratios of 4-8 give the same factor of reduction over MHA. C is correct: this is the empirical motivation for GQA (better quality than MQA at slightly higher memory). B is wrong: total attention FLOPs per token do not shrink because each query head still computes a full Q@K^T against its shared K (the same total number of multiply-adds; only the memory reads are shared). D is wrong: GQA can be initialized from an MHA checkpoint by averaging or replicating KV projections and then finetuned briefly.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: 'uptraining' from MHA to GQA is a documented practice.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: FLOPs are unchanged; only KV bandwidth/storage shrinks.

assumptions: G divides H evenly; each group of H/G query heads shares one KV head.
Discussion is inference decode compute/memory, not training.
nonImplications: Does not imply GQA always matches MHA quality; it is a compromise.
Does not imply that any G value is optimal; the choice depends on model scale and data.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses memory reduction with FLOP reduction.

performanceClaim.scope: GQA memory reduction and quality trade-off vs MHA/MQA
